```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"

```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(rscprep)
library(Seurat)
```

`seuratFrom10x()` handles the two shapes 10x Cell Ranger output actually comes
in -- standard single-sample `cellranger count` runs, and demuxed
`cellranger multi` runs -- behind one interface, so downstream code doesn't
need to branch on which one it's looking at.

You can point it at a single sample or run directly, or hand it a manifest
describing a batch of runs from either pipeline. Either way, it returns a
named list of Seurat objects, one per sample, ready to merge or process
independently.

The `multi` argument is the one thing you have to get right, and it asks
which *pipeline* wrote the directory -- not whether samples were pooled. See
"Choosing `multi`" below if the run came off `cellranger multi` with a single
sample in it, which is the usual shape for Flex and 5'.

```{r, child = "_heart1k.Rmd"}
```

## A `cellranger count` run

```{r single-sample}
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path  = outs,
  multi = FALSE
)

seurat_list$heart_1k_v3
```

`path` should point to the Cell Ranger `outs/` directory -- the function
looks for `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` directly inside it. The sample name
is inferred from the parent folder (`heart_1k_v3`, one level up from `outs`).

That object has 957 cells, not the 1,011 in `heart1k`. The defaults
`min.cells = 10` and `min.features = 50` are passed to
`Seurat::CreateSeuratObject()`, and with only ~2,000 genes in the bundled
matrix, 54 cells fall under 50 detected genes. `heart1k` was built with both
set to 0 so it keeps every cell Cell Ranger called:

```{r no-filters}
seuratFrom10x(path = outs, multi = FALSE, min.cells = 0, min.features = 0)
```

## A `cellranger multi` run

The bundled data comes from `cellranger count`, so the next two examples use
placeholder paths and are not run.

```{r multi-run, eval = FALSE}
seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(
  path  = "/path/to/Pool1/outs",
  multi = TRUE
)

names(seurat_list)
#> [1] "Bleo_18_Slim_10" "Bleo_22_Slim_14" ...
```

For `cellranger multi` output, one `outs/` directory holds every demuxed
sample under `per_sample_outs/<sample>/`. `seuratFrom10x()` reads each
sample's `count/sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` separately and returns
one Seurat object per demuxed sample -- a single function call here returns a
list, not a single object.

## A batch of runs via manifest

```{r manifest-batch, eval = FALSE}
manifest <- data.frame(
  Path = c(
    "/path/to/Sample_1/outs",
    "/path/to/Sample_2/outs",
    "/path/to/Pool1/outs"
  ),
  multi = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

seurat_list <- seuratFrom10x(manifest = manifest, min.cells = 3, min.features = 200)
```

The manifest needs a `Path` column (each row's `outs/` directory) and a
logical `multi` column. Rows can mix the two pipelines freely -- each row is
resolved independently, and a `multi = TRUE` row expands into one entry per
demuxed sample in the returned list. If a sample's expected H5 file is
missing, that row is skipped with a warning rather than failing the whole
batch; single-path mode fails immediately instead, since there's nothing left
to fall back on.

## Choosing `multi`

`multi` picks between two directory layouts, and the two Cell Ranger
pipelines write different ones:

| `multi` | Pipeline | Where the filtered H5 lives |
|---|---|---|
| `FALSE` | `cellranger count` | `outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` |
| `TRUE` | `cellranger multi` | `outs/per_sample_outs/<sample>/count/sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` |

The question is which pipeline ran, not how many samples came out of it.
`cellranger multi` writes `per_sample_outs/` even when it demultiplexed
exactly one sample -- routine for Flex and 5' -- so those runs need
`multi = TRUE` despite not being multiplexed in any biological sense. If you
are unsure, look for `per_sample_outs/` inside `outs/`: if it is there, the
run needs `multi = TRUE`.

This argument used to be called `multiplexed`, which read as a claim about
the experiment rather than about the pipeline. The old name still works and
warns.

## Notes

`min.cells` and `min.features` are passed straight through to
`Seurat::CreateSeuratObject()` and apply uniformly across every sample in a
batch -- set them once at the level of granularity you actually want, not
per-sample.
